promptDigestNote: The dispatch supplied a subject digest but no prompt digest, so I measured the prompt three times at start and again at end to detect motion during review. It held.
summary: Subject and prompt held. This is an evaluation rule rather than an application, so I read what it permits before what it refuses. It permits nothing today: it marks no row SATISFIED, edits no cell, and its eligibility test is five conjunctive gates whose fourth is a dedicated later D-000 cycle with independent SATISFIED-GRADE review of that specific row. What it changes is where execution evidence sits, and the structural question is whether that lets anything ship earlier. It does not — clause 1 keeps execution, QUALIFIED and DEMONSTRATED in condition 4 / DR-012, and file 08 gates condition 5 on conditions 1, 2 and 4, so the execution gate is relocated rather than removed. The narrowness is demonstrated rather than asserted: I expanded the entry's shorthand row lists and all thirty condition-2 rows are accounted for, with eighteen named ineligible and reasons given for the five closest calls.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: d4b628f6c8b860c65e2d1ca3f063caeae090b2358e0f468fa1b29ced72bdae49, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at ac67c2b4… across start and end.

The grant, read first and on its own terms. Eligibility requires all five of: Class A or Class B standing; every remaining acceptance-evidence member being only harness execution, fixture execution or qualification measurement; each remainder already named as a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner; a dedicated later D-000 cycle plus independent SATISFIED-GRADE review of that row; and an MF-6 cell edit. Clause 2 states 'This entry marks no row SATISFIED' and clause 4 'Does not rewrite live cells'. So the rule authorises a future path with its own gates, not an outcome now.

The structural question — whether relocating execution lets implementation start earlier — resolves against the attack. Clause 1 states 'Execution, QUALIFIED, and DEMONSTRATED remain condition 4 / DR-012. They are not architecture SATISFIED evidence.' file 08's condition-5 row reads 'Not started; structurally last, and gated on 1, 2 and 4', and condition 4 currently stands PARTLY MET with 'no gate names a concrete harness artifact'. So even if eligible rows later become SATISFIED without execution, condition 5 still cannot open until condition 4 carries that execution. The rule reallocates evidence between conditions; it does not remove a gate.

DR-012 is the right anchor for that reallocation. Its row reads 'Product is not release-qualified' under the Product/release authority, and D-001 states 'DR-012 is not a blueprint-entry prerequisite; it remains mandatory before release or authoritative launch.' Placing execution there is consistent with D-001's own separation of blueprint entry from release qualification.

The deadlock the entry claims to resolve is real on the register's own terms: condition 2 requires SATISFIED, DR-102's cell makes SATISFIED wait on execution, execution is condition-4 qualification, and condition 5 — which any harness implementation would need — is gated on 1, 2 and 4. The entry does not resolve it by fiat but by separating architecture evidence from qualification evidence while keeping both mandatory.

The attack 'Class B silently SATISFIES DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED rows' fails, and I checked it by lead label rather than by text mention. Exactly five rows carry DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED as their lead label — DR-104, DR-115, DR-118, DR-119, DR-123 — matching file 08's condition-2 count of five. The entry names three as eligible in kind and expressly excludes the other two with reasons: DR-104 for negative-test corpus authoring, DR-118 for thresholds remaining UNDECIDED. Class B does not sweep its own label.

A sixth row, DR-103, mentions DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED in its cell text but its lead label is OPEN, which is why the register counts five and why the entry treats DR-103 under Class A reasoning instead. Its stated ineligibility — 'Fixture authoring plus independent review remain' — matches file 08's own 'design contract ACCEPTED 2026-08-13 (D-013); the fixture-corpus half…'.

The row accounting is complete. Expanding the entry's 'DR-101 / 107 / 111 / …' shorthand, it names all thirty DR-1xx rows that file 08 carries, with none unaccounted and none named that is not a row. Four are eligible in kind, five are named ineligible with individual reasons, twelve are excluded for having no accepted T2-02 contract or DECIDED measurement-only leftover, and nine are assigned to condition 2's deferral limb.

The attack 'applies the split to DR-103 while fixture authoring remains' fails: DR-103 is in the ineligible table, and clause 5 reinforces it — 'DR-103's own schema already places fixture generation under DR-120 / DR-G15. That authoring must exist and be independently reviewed before DR-103 can become eligible.'

The attack 'applies the split to DR-118 while thresholds remain UNDECIDED' fails: DR-118 is in the ineligible table and rejected again in the alternatives. file 08's DR-118 cell confirms the premise, reading 'thresholds remain UNDECIDED (unlike DR-115)' — the parenthetical also independently supports DR-115's Class B placement.

Every supporting citation resolves to what the entry says it does. D-013 records alternative (b) as 'Coin a new status label (the turn-1 draft proposed DESIGN-ACCEPTED) — rejected: D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03…'; D-006's NOTE-03 reads 'the closed status vocabulary stays closed; coining an analog would itself be a register-content decision'; D-015 concerns CC-1..CC-11 stranded at a gate; D-008 is 'DR-119 acceptance: self-contained language-closure product rule'; D-009 is 'DR-123 acceptance: mandatory CLI baseline'; D-035 records doctor-contract.v4 as DR-114's accepted design contract; and D-042 records permission-truth-tables.v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract *candidate* — which is precisely why the entry rules DR-105 ineligible, 'D-042 recorded v2 as a candidate, not as an accepted T2-02 contract'. That distinction is exact.

All thirteen cited decisions — D-001, D-002, D-006, D-008, D-009, D-010, D-012, D-013, D-015, D-035, D-042, D-070, D-084 — are present in COORD and ADOPTED. D-056 is not yet present, so adoption creates no collision.

The attack 'coins DESIGN-ACCEPTED or another file-08 status token' fails. I swept every all-caps token in the subject: SATISFIED, OPEN, DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, QUALIFIED, DEMONSTRATED, UNDECIDED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, MEASUREMENT, RULE-GOVERNED, SATISFIED-GRADE and DESIGN-ACCEPTED. All are existing vocabulary; SATISFIED-GRADE is a review-verdict term rather than a file-08 status; and DESIGN-ACCEPTED appears only inside refusals — the header's 'Does not coin DESIGN-ACCEPTED', clause 9, and the alternatives, which leave it available to a later dedicated vocabulary decision.

The attack 'extends D-070's qualifying-set union to condition 2' fails: clause 8 states 'Condition 2 continues to be counted from leading SATISFIED labels plus explicit deferral dispositions, not from this rule existing', the preamble states D-070's algorithm is condition-1 only, and the alternatives reject treating the preview-note union as a condition-2 count.

The attacks 'this entry marks rows SATISFIED', 'amends D-001', 'treats harness naming as SATISFIED', 'treats execution as architecture SATISFIED', 'silent deferral of condition 2', 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' and 'file 08 edited' all fail on explicit clauses: the header's five refusals, clause 2's 'Coordinator fiat remains unlawful (DR-204)', clause 3's 'condition 2 remains NOT MET. Zero SATISFIED is added', Eligibility (3)'s 'Naming a harness identifier is not itself SATISFIED', clause 6's 'Deferred D-002 / D-010 items stay on the deferral limb', clause 7's 'Condition 5 remains last', and the readiness effect 'Zero at adoption. No SATISFIED. No blueprint. Condition 2 stays NOT MET.' file 08 measures at its cited digest and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.

All four measured inputs match live bytes: COORD eec2f966…, file 08 ff2ebadd…, the freeze and claim-register.v1. Both commits resolve: 242dbe34 'D-084: file-08 note for DR-011 parent owner recording' and e40b3f19 'D-070: adopt file-08 MF-6 notes for preview owner recordings'. The file 08 pin is the post-D-084 value, and I confirmed that edit landed — the preamble now reads 'one SATISFIED and ten explicitly disposed' and the replacement summary paragraph is present — so the entry's premise that condition 1 is MET for preview scope is true of the current register.

The entry introduces no statement that goes stale, because it edits nothing: clause 4 keeps today's cells authoritative and defers every rewrite to later per-row MF-6 acts. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.

Whether each of the four motivating candidates would actually pass Eligibility (2) on a full audit of its remaining evidence members. The entry says they are eligible 'in kind' and requires a dedicated cycle per row; I verified the class placements and the stated leftovers against file 08 but did not enumerate every acceptance-evidence member of DR-102, DR-115, DR-119 or DR-123.

Whether the twelve rows excluded for having no accepted T2-02 contract genuinely lack one. I confirmed the partition covers all thirty rows and spot-checked the five closest calls; I did not audit each of the twelve.
Whether the nine rows assigned to the deferral limb are correctly deferred under D-002 / D-010. The entry routes them away from this rule rather than disposing of them.

Whether harness execution necessarily requires docs/v2/implementation/. The deadlock argument depends on it, and condition 4's 'no gate names a concrete harness artifact' supports it, but I did not establish that no lawful execution path exists outside that directory.

The merits of the design contracts the rule would rely on — control-protocol-contract.v2, doctor-contract.v4, permission-truth-tables.v2 and the rest — beyond confirming what their recording decisions say about their standing.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of subject and prompt three times at start and again at end with ls -l for permissions; digest verification of all four measured inputs against live bytes; git log --format=%s at full hash for both commits; expansion of the entry's 'DR-101 / 107 / …' shorthand into a full row set for comparison against every DR-1xx row in file 08, establishing complete coverage of the thirty condition-2 rows; per-row lead-label extraction to identify which rows carry DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED as a label rather than a mention, resolving the five-versus-six count and testing Class B's scope; verbatim check of file 08's SATISFIED legend against the entry's quotation; extraction of the DR-102, DR-103, DR-118 and DR-012 rows and of the condition-4 and condition-5 rows to test the deadlock premise and the relocation argument; targeted extraction from COORD of D-013's alternative (b), D-006's NOTE-03, D-015's CC-1..CC-11 passage, and the titles of D-008, D-009, D-035 and D-042 to test each citation against its actual subject; register-standing checks for all thirteen cited decisions plus a D-056 collision check; an all-caps token sweep of the subject to test for a coined status token; occurrence counts of every refusal clause; git status across docs/v2/architecture and the tree

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. This is the first entry in this sequence that changes how a readiness condition is evidenced rather than recording a particular artifact, so I read the grant before the refusals and asked the structural question directly: does moving execution out of architecture evidence let anything ship earlier. It does not, because condition 5 is gated on condition 4 as well as condition 2, and the entry keeps execution, QUALIFIED and DEMONSTRATED firmly in condition 4 / DR-012 — which D-001 itself separates from blueprint entry. The narrowness is demonstrated rather than claimed: expanding the shorthand, all thirty condition-2 rows are accounted for, eighteen are ruled out, and the five closest calls each carry a reason that matches the register. The one I checked hardest was DR-105, because a design-contract recording could easily have been read as an accepted contract — and the entry gets it right, resting the exclusion on D-042 having recorded a candidate rather than a T2-02 acceptance.
